objective: At each fit, the existing feature-increment requests at the visit's own feed-forward merge (33 or 34) plus original-correct member/place/prompt error in the same continuous direction-and-size sum; current text and registration. Dose, from step 2 on: the builder targets at BOTH feed-forward 33 and feed-forward 34, each made from the visit-start state on its current histories before the walk and held fixed for that step, full correct-member answer error at all 105 merges and the local correct prompt error. row_requests.construction: Current registered input features plus the fixed original-support increment, prepared by loop_requests.py separately for each visit.
row_requests.site: The current visit's own feed-forward merge: 33 at step 1 and at the odd steps, 34 at the even ones.
row_requests.support_note: All seven supports stand, discovery-15-channel-h1 among them, as in the primary chain. At this run's one link, feed-forward 33, 12 of the fourteen builders rest mostly on that support in the step-3 reading; it is 8 J under the regime's boundary, and Performance's card-1 direct terms put its feed-forward-33 term at -1.70 beside -2.73 to -5.03 for the other six. Kept as descriptions: no margin and no projected difference becomes a multiplier, an exclusion or a target, and no auxiliary observation becomes a support.
row_requests.correspondence: Incoming means at the CURRENT registration's declared place; nearest mixture of the fixed original seven supports. All current rows in the cell contribute. This is computational correspondence, not a semantic certificate.
row_requests.native_execution: The request same-line-sign-original kept was measured on the registered recordings. Each link's request is made in the reading its solve's rows are in (controlled-bf16-4's passes, as generated, card 0): the builders' incoming states from the link's own rows, the supports' states before and after the merge and every row's origin from the original file's own reading in that same execution (controlled-bf16-1/baseline, which every solve counts from). Link 33's is compared with the recordings' request and the difference recorded; the recordings' file is kept as it is.
row_requests.exclusions: No case has two answers among the builders and supports. discovery-10-channel-h1 (a builder) and discovery-10-channel-h3 (a correct member) answer one question and are kept in one fold.
row_requests.unsupported_cells: Every registered place and prompt position of the fifteen wrong fitting members except the fourteen builders' sign rows: no target is known there and none is invented; they carry no term and are not called agreement. Among them the sign row of expanded-001-h3. All thirty are in the outcome reading.

hypothesis: Refreshing rows and feature-increment requests on each actual current history, with whole-own-trace member feedback before retaining a stage, permits repeated correction against the original rather than continuing a fit on stale histories.
why_this_direction: The agreed on-policy loop fell out of active tracking. A/B showed that held-text local improvement did not establish own-path repair, and crossed readings attributed 0.97–1.03 of pooled L's rise to wording. The current bridge and own-history dose instruments now make its smallest site-33 test executable; original full-path measurements, not candidate outcomes, supplied this site and support set.
repeating_pattern_check: Earlier constructions optimized a supplied history then read the new one only after the full edit. Pooled means concealed member motion and a radius made a no-cost interior. Here every compared stage gets its own histories, the score is continuous member error, and changed text triggers refresh rather than exclusion. Transport of original correct targets across rewording is explicitly still an experimental assumption.
what_went_wrong_before: The loop was omitted from tracking; the new request consumer initially expected own_compare metadata rather than own_text's actual record, and own-text prompt origins would have targeted zero. a18ce27d repairs these interfaces. A score alone still cannot certify correspondence or capability repair.

rule.scope: A bounded two-site current-history construction at feed-forward 33 and 34, not proof of whole-capability repair and not the whole merged plan (plan v4's answer-level target over more of the path is unfinished work). No no-fit or reserved evaluation. Step 1 is the one-site visit at 33 as it was declared and made.
rule.requests: row_requests.refresh=current registration; all current rows at the declared place, equal Layout coefficients, original support increments and original anchors. No target is inferred from generated words. From step 2 on the request is made at the visit's own merge and, for the dose, at the other matrix's merge too: both from the visit-start state on the same current histories, before the walk (row_requests.read_at; steps/<n>/asked.npz and steps/<n>/sites/<matrix>/asked.npz).
rule.dose: All distinct BF16 stage ends through the recomputed reference unit, plus unchanged. Read all fitting members on each stage's own text at every merge. Same member score on held fold and full cohort; choose least held score among stages strictly improving both; smaller actual matrix change breaks an exact tie. From step 2 on every score keeps the builders' request cells at both feed-forward 33 and feed-forward 34 at the existing per-cell normalization: no division by the number of sites and no balancing coefficient; the active site's targets are the solve's own asked targets. A missing required correspondence is unresolved. A compact reading follows records/retrospectives/2026-11-14-compact-dose-astra.md; an unqualified or non-equivalent reading takes the full path.
rule.continuation: Write the selected stage, refresh the written state's histories, registration, rows and requests, and visit the next matrix. A visit that selects no stage keeps its start, and the loop moves on to the next matrix. A complete pass over the loop's matrices that keeps every start ends this bounded construction. Missing required coverage, an invalid capture, missing provenance or a failed execution ends as unresolved/instrument failure: it is neither convergence nor that stopping condition. Every visit compares its stages with its own unchanged start only; scores of different visits use different requests and starts and are not one error curve. A state met again exactly is recorded as a cycle.
rule.acceptance: The score is construction validation, not the capability verdict. Full own trace, every answer, missing targets and correspondence are reported; no complete repair claim while a gap, a new correct discrepancy or an undefined correspondence remains. Answer outputs are descriptions, never the selector.
rule.reference: The original correct reference, original support transformations and normalization remain fixed. Original correct target transport after rewording is a hypothesis, not established semantic equivalence.
rule.order: Step 1 at blk.33.ffn_down.weight (made). Step 2 at blk.34.ffn_down.weight, step 3 at blk.33.ffn_down.weight, and so on in turn: loop.matrices, step n at the n-th counted round and round. A step starts from the state the steps before it left: the last written state, on the text that state itself writes.
rule.folds: The fold held out of a step's walk is (step - 1) modulo the number of case folds, in the existing fold order (parameters.fold_schedule; loop.held_folds writes it out for the driver).
rule.sources: From step 2 on a step's commands are made only by the files `solver` names: the step driver holds loop.py, tube.py, correction.py and loop_requests.py to their hashes before the step and before its walk, and the scorer before its visit (visit_outcome.py --sources). A change of one of them is a revision here first.

The switch is this declaration's and no shell's (read_loop_visit.py takes it from here).

coordinates_and_weights.derivation: The frozen reference's scales S_direction 1268.5365669493656 and S_size 28.67797931944294: a form weighs w_f = 0.5/S_f, 3.9415e-04 for the direction and 1.7435e-02 for the size, the same at every merge, place and link. The joint features' size coordinate is the log size times the root of w_size/w_direction (6.6508510517827295).
coordinates_and_weights.scales_with: The original model, its full original reference and the native terminal transform. Another source needs its own reference.

request_target.derivation: The step-3 run fixes who is asked and against whom (its fourteen builders, seven supports, each one's sign row) and the construction; its kept request at this merge has lengths 0.062 to 0.195 at feed-forward 33. This run's own request is made by correction.asked from the rows the link reads and the original file's reading, as `rule.request` says, and recorded with its hash and its distance from the kept one. Nothing of it is scaled, capped or rounded.
request_target.scales_with: The supports, the correspondence at each link's incoming state, the merge, the prefix and the text of the answers.

request_rows.derivation: The frozen registration lays each of the fourteen builders' sign rows alone at place 168 (checked again by correction.asked at every link of this run): at that place a builder's mean is its one row, so the request asked of the member there is the row's own.

request_weight.derivation: A request weighs the reference's own cell of the wrong group at that merge and place, w_f, over the number of wrong members among the answers summed over: 10 on the two folds a path is solved on, 5 on the fold it is read on, 15 for the last solve (fourteen requests, each at w_f/15). Not rebalanced by margin, support, parameter count or number of rows (Astra).
request_weight.scales_with: The reference's weights and the number of wrong members in each sum.

correct_member_weight.derivation: A correct member's squared own error at a place weighs w_f/n_c with n_c the number of correct members among the answers summed over: 11, 9 and 10 on the pairs of folds solved on, 4, 6 and 5 on the folds read, 15 for the last solve. The group's own cell is left out, so this is counted once.
correct_member_weight.scales_with: The reference's weights and the number of correct members in each sum.

prompt_position_weight.derivation: One prompt position of a correct member weighs what one registered answer place of that member weighs, w_f/n_c: the convention that diagnostic exercised and Astra's specification of the member objective kept. A convention between two units, named as one, and no multiplier to tune.
prompt_position_weight.scales_with: The reference's weights, the number of correct members summed over, and each prompt's number of positions.

ridge_unit.derivation: Per link, correction.unit_of on the reference's unmodified cells at the matrix the link starts from over all thirty fitting answers' rows that link keeps: the trace of the direction cells' action on the inputs times the mean squared learned scale, plus the size cells' curvature trace over the output width, over the input width. Computed by each link's command and recorded; no value from another matrix or link is used. A scale the search is counted in, not a claim about the sum's curvature.
ridge_unit.scales_with: The link's rows, the matrix's shape (12288 by 1536), the learned merge scale and the reference's weights.

first_ridge.derivation: Per link, the largest power of two times the unit not above 2||s||^2/(RESOLVED x E), with E the whole sum on all thirty at the link's start and s the slope of E/2 there (correction.strongest). Computed by each link's command and recorded with its inputs.
first_ridge.scales_with: The link's requests, where the prefix has left the correct members, the initial slope, the unit and the arithmetic's resolution.

ridge_spacing.derivation: The solver halves the ridge from one stage to the next (PATH = 1), each stage starting from the last written state. The search's grain, the same for every matrix; a valley between two powers can be missed, and the record keeps every stage.
ridge_spacing.scales_with: Nothing of the data: a finer grain costs proportionally more stages.

work_limits.derivation: The solver's own constants as each record keeps them (tube.EFFORT: at most 40 accepted rounds a stage, and 400 conjugate-gradient iterations a round's linear solve, as 10 passes of 40 where cells have radii and one run of 400 where none has; RESOLVED, the root of float32's rounding, ends a stage whose round falls by no more than that part of its starting sum). They were set on the solver's calibration at other matrices and are not measured for these: they limit work and do not shape the sum. Whether they bind is recorded per stage; a stage that ends at a limit is work not finished and no statement about what a longer solve would reach.
work_limits.scales_with: The local curvature at each matrix and the ridge.

second_ridge.derivation: No number: at each round the second ridge is (the sum at the solved step, read with every rounding on the way to the layer's last merge holding what it added at the round's matrix, less the first-order model's value there) over the step's squared length, when that difference is more than RESOLVED of the sum, and the step is solved again where it exceeds the one it was solved with; it only rises along a path. Named here from step 2 on, before any walk of it. Step 1's walk was made under 'measured' and stands as made; walked again with the roundings held it is the record's path at every stage its visit scored (records/development/2026-11-12-correction-objective/README.md, "The loop's step 1 walked again with the roundings held"). Why this reading: read through the merges themselves, the difference took the engine's BF16 rounding for curvature and froze a path: the primary chain's link 33 kept 0.999970 of its held start and its link 34 0.815 under 'measured', where the same links solved with the roundings held kept 0.497 and 0.353.
second_ridge.scales_with: How far the merges depart from their first order at a step with the roundings held, which depends on the matrix, the ridge and the step; and, for what the reading leaves out on purpose, how many rows the engine reads several tokens at once (the question's positions and each answer's first step) and how strongly the per-layer embedding's path reaches the layer's last merge.

step_acceptance.derivation: Each BF16-written trial is read through the native merge expression on every row and taken only when the whole sum E on the answers solved on is strictly less; otherwise the part of the step is halved down to no written movement. No bound and no held reading vetoes a step; held folds choose the setting only.
step_acceptance.scales_with: The file's BF16 grid and the proposed change.

solve_geometry.derivation: The eigenbasis that speeds a round's linear solves and the measure a writing is nearest in are made from the reference's unmodified cells on the rows solved on (correction.basis_of). The action is a gram of one row of inputs a cell, so its rank is at most the number of cells of the merges read (1,920 here) whatever the width; Performance measured 1,732 values above what a double factoring resolves, of at most 1,920, at a 6144-wide feed-forward matrix (the record named) and 958 of at most 960 at attention 17, 2,048 wide (the record beside it). The linear solve and the measure use the eigenvectors of the 1,920 largest values and the ridge alone on every other direction: the same operator, not a truncation by size. They change how fast a solve arrives and which BF16 neighbour a writing prefers, not what is solved.
solve_geometry.scales_with: The rows solved on, the reference's weights and the number of places and merges read.

dose_and_stopping.derivation: Continuous member squared direction/log-size error, summed at the original form weights and divided by each original group's count in the subset. The same fixed per-step targets score all stages. Strictly lower held and full sums are the algebraic improvement condition; no numerical tolerance. Equal held scores choose smaller actual BF16 change.
dose_and_stopping.scales_with: The declared coverage, original scales, current histories, and group membership in each existing fitting fold.

fold_schedule.derivation: Use correction.case_folds on the existing source fitting folds; held index=(step-1) modulo the number of those folds. Earlier steps can have trained a later held member, so these are construction data, not independent validation.
fold_schedule.scales_with: The number and membership of the existing case-family folds.

last_ridge.derivation: Compute correction.unit_of from current rows and the fixed reference for each visit. Stop the first bounded path when ridge equals that measured unit: power zero, inclusive. This is a declared work boundary for repeated feedback, not an inferred optimum; the older sign paths selected weaker ridges.
last_ridge.scales_with: Current input geometry and original reference scales; the boundary is recomputed, not borrowed as a matrix-specific ridge value.

matrices.derivation: The decision is records/retrospectives/2026-11-14-multi-matrix-loop-astra.md. What it rests on, from step 1's own records at 18 of 18 stages: the walk's own reading of the cells it is asked at and the whole model's on the stage's own text agree for the wrong group to 4.5e-06 of the start, and all of the difference between the two readings is the correct group's, at merges the fit at 33 does not read; from 2^7 (the least held score, 0.9705) to 2^0 the change of the matrix grows 25.22-fold, that difference 94.4-fold and the builders' gain 11.40-fold. Of the correct members' rise, 0.5238 to 0.9986 lies at layer 34's three merges, after the solver's two (dose_split.py, same folder). Feed-forward 34 is the one matrix whose solve reads every merge its change reaches on a fixed text (its own merge and the model's last, as the output norm passes it on); feed-forward 33 is the site the first visit corrected. Not chosen from any candidate's outcome, and no claim that these are the only sites.
matrices.scales_with: Which merges lie behind a matrix and outside its solve's reading, and how the cost there grows with the step: one more matrix to the loop where a later visit shows the same.

sites_read.derivation: The loop's matrices, each one's builder request cells in every score whichever matrix is fit, so that a visit at one site cannot lower its score by giving up what the other site's requests gained. From step 2: the first step made after the decision. Step 1 was scored before it at its one site.
sites_read.scales_with: The loop's matrices: one request set a matrix.

prediction: At least one distinct BF16 stage in a visit reduces the same declared own-history objective on its held fitting fold and the entire fitting cohort; after retaining it, a subsequent visit can be prepared from the written state's own text, fresh rows and original-support request without stale offsets. Whole-trace and per-answer readings are reported regardless.
would_weaken_it: No stage lowers both readings within the declared path; refreshed targets have unresolved correspondence; the score falls while an own full-trace discrepancy or new correct-member failure remains; or the next visit cannot be formed from the exact written state. Any such result is retained, not a reason to relabel sign counts or change thresholds.

At step 1 the walk's own held reading promised more than the whole model kept (0.4702 of its start by the walk at 2^0, 0.9705 at the least stage the visit read): the visit, not the walk, selects, and the next matrix is the one whose solve reads what its change reaches. continuation.hypothesis: A correction spread over the two last feed-forwards in small steps, each fit on the current state's own text and kept only where the whole model's reading lowers both sums, keeps more of the builders' requests than the one step at 33 kept, at less cost to the correct answers.
prediction: At feed-forward 34, on the stages that leave every answer's text as it was, the walk's own reading of the held correct members and the visit's differ from their starts by the same amount (no merge lies behind the solver's two there), as they did for the wrong group at 33.
The visit at 34 selects a stage that keeps less of its held start than the 0.9705 step 1 kept at 33.
The 33 request cells in a score of the visit at 34 move only where a stage rewords an answer.
continuation.would_weaken_it: At 34 the two readings part for the correct group on unchanged text by what they parted at 33 (then the reading of that difference is wrong); no stage at 34 lowers both sums; or the pass 34 then 33 keeps both starts, which ends this construction with step 1's state.
